title: Erlang Bit Syntax (<<Val:Size/TypeSpecifiers>>): Bit-Level Protocol Packing & Endianness
solutionExplanation: Demonstrates <<V:4, F:4, L:16/big>> packing, pattern matching with trailing binary capture, and length-prefixed encoding.

typesSpec: TypeSpecifiers = integer | binary | big | little | utf8
otpDocCards.description: Declarative bit-level data packing and destructuring.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: Executed using hardware vector instructions in ERTS.

mentalModelCheck.question: What is the binary representation of <<4:4, 2:4, 1024:16/big>>?

options.label: <<66, 4, 0>> (0x42 = 0100 0010 = 66, and 1024 in 16-bit big-endian is 0x0400 = 4, 0)
options.explanation: 4 (0100) and 2 (0010) pack into the first byte (01000010 = 66); 1024 is high byte 4 and low byte 0.
4 and 2 are 4-bit nibbles that pack together into a single 8-bit byte.
<<66, 0, 4>> would be little-endian; big-endian places the high byte 4 first.
